assertions.text: The impact of the break on the work-optional date is stated as a range or under more than one named scenario, not as a single revised date.
assertions.evidence: §1 table: "Break, re-enter $150k Sept 2029 | late 2036 (age 48) | mid 2039 (age 51)"; "Break, re-enter $130k ... late 2037 | early 2041", plus §9 Scenario D "2.5% real, $130,000 re-entry, six-month search: early 2042, age 53."

assertions.text: Outcomes are reported under at least two different investment-return assumptions, one materially more conservative than the base case.
assertions.evidence: §1 table columns "4.5% real | 2.5% real": no break "late 2032 | early 2034"; break at $150k "late 2036 | mid 2039"; $130k "late 2037 | early 2041". Both rates recur in §3 balances, §9 A/B scenarios, and §10's 12-month option.

assertions.text: Statutory or regulatory figures quoted in the document (tax brackets or deductions, contribution limits, subsidy or poverty-line thresholds, penalty rules) each carry a source and the date they were checked.
assertions.evidence: Figures carry a year label but no source and no check date: "Standard deduction $16,100; 0% LTCG ceiling $49,450... Colorado flat 4.4%"; "Federal poverty level, single = $16,000 | 2026 guideline, rounded". No IRS/HHS/statute citation anywhere; footer only defers to "confirmed... November 2027".

assertions.text: The document names which accounts fund the break and in what order.
assertions.evidence: §5 "Which accounts pay, in what order": "**The order is: HYSA → taxable brokerage → Roth contribution basis → (never) 401(k).**" followed by per-account amounts and rationale ("1. HYSA — $101,907, covers everything", "2. Taxable brokerage — $182,039, the free reserve", "3. Roth IRA contribution basis — $54,000").

assertions.text: The funding plan either avoids early-withdrawal penalties on retirement accounts or, where a penalized withdrawal is contemplated, states the penalty and tax cost explicitly.
assertions.evidence: "The order is: HYSA → taxable brokerage → Roth contribution basis → (never) 401(k)." Plus explicit math: "10% early-distribution penalty | 3,000 | Federal income tax (taxable $13,900) | 1,420 | Colorado 4.4% | 612 | Total | 5,032 — 16.8%", and stacked case "12,176 — 40.6%".

assertions.text: Health coverage is priced for all 24 months of the break; no part of the break period is left with unpriced or unspecified coverage.
assertions.evidence: Budget covers every month: "Travel medical, Aug–Dec 2027 (5 mo @ $110) 550 | Travel medical, Jan–Mar 2028 (3 mo @ $110) 330 | ... Marketplace silver + CSR, 2028 (12 mo @ $126) 1,512 | Marketplace silver + CSR, Jan–Aug 2029 (8 mo @ $126) 1,008" — plus dental/vision "24 months" and evac "2 years"; total $9,800.

assertions.text: The document evaluates using the low-income break years for Roth conversion or capital-gains harvesting, reaching a stated recommendation (doing either, or explicitly not, with a reason).
assertions.evidence: §7 "Roth conversions and 0% capital-gains harvesting": "**Convert $28,000 to Roth in 2028.** It's worth about $1,000 more than harvesting" — with reason ("2028 is your only clean low-income year"), a not-do ("Converting past the subsidy band is worse than not converting at all"; "**2029: do neither**").

assertions.text: The document connects the size or source of withdrawals and conversions during the break to health-insurance subsidy eligibility (income thresholds), rather than treating the two as independent.
assertions.evidence: §7: "Converting to the top of the 12% bracket means $66,500 of MAGI. That's 416% of FPL — over the cliff, so the premium tax credit goes to zero"; §5 401(k): "Lost premium tax credit (MAGI goes 175% → 362% FPL) | 4,266"; Roth basis "doesn't raise your MAGI, so it doesn't touch your health insurance subsidy."

assertions.text: The planning horizon extends to at least age 95.
assertions.evidence: No mention of age 95 or longevity anywhere. Every "95" is dollars ($95,160 break cost, "$95,000 gate"). The longest horizon modelled is the 59½ bridge: "you only need to bridge 10.8 years to August 2047." Portfolio survival past 59½ to 95 is never tested.

assertions.text: Downside outcomes are described in terms of what Maya would actually live on or do differently (spending level, break shortened, working longer), not solely as a portfolio survival or success percentage.
assertions.evidence: Downside = behavior, not survival %: "Cut Phase A short by 2 months"; "Cut Phase C from 10 months to 5"; "End the break in April 2029; start the search immediately"; and "two years of freedom at 39–41, bought for roughly four years... at 48 instead of 44. In the worst modelled case, 53 instead of 46."

assertions.text: The document states at least one if-then rule with a numeric trigger and a defined checkpoint for delaying departure or cutting the break short.
assertions.evidence: Gate 1, "check 1 June 2027": "HYSA balance | ≥ $95,000 ... Delay notice one quarter per $12,000 short". Gate 2: "1 Aug 2028 (12 mo) | 57,446 | $48,000 | Cut Phase C from 10 months to 5." Dated checkpoints, numeric thresholds, delay/cut-short actions.

assertions.text: The document shows the effect on the plan of re-entering work later than planned or at lower pay than the base assumption.
assertions.evidence: §9 tables both futures: "At $130k | late **2037** | early **2041** | **Cost of the $20k** | **+1.0 yr** | **+1.8 yr**" and Scenario B six-month search → "$150k, six-month search | mid **2037** | early **2040**", plus "months 26–31 come from the brokerage… end with about **$177,600**".

assertions.text: The asset figures the document is built on agree, within rounding, with the balances in Maya's own records.
assertions.evidence: §3 opening column: 401(k) 412,000 · Roth 88,500 · Taxable 174,200 · HYSA 46,800 · HSA 19,300 · "Total 740,800" — matches accounts-2026-07.txt line for line, as does model.py's "K401, ROTH, TAXABLE, HYSA, HSA = 412_000, 88_500, 174_200, 46_800, 19_300"; basis $54,000/$121,000 also match.

assertions.text: The document names at least one specific item for Maya to verify with a licensed professional or the relevant official body — beyond a generic advice disclaimer.
assertions.evidence: Closing note: "Premium and FPL figures are estimates to be confirmed at Connect for Health Colorado during open enrolment in November 2027." Also §11: "Confirm 401(k) vesting schedule — any cliff between now and July 2027 (A14)" / A14 "Check the plan document."
